extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners (prosecution attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when a patent application is considered abandoned or terminated and the substantive requirements for seeking withdrawal of a holding of abandonment or revival under 37 CFR 1.137 (unavoidable/unintentional delay), including required replies, fees, terminal disclaimers, and evidentiary showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated circumstances that may cause an application to become abandoned (examples A–I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes failure to reply to the last Office action; withdrawal of or failure to prosecute an appeal to the Board; dismissal of an appeal to the Court of Appeals or civil action without a timely responsive amendment; claims suggested for interference near the end of the reply period; filing under former 37 CFR 1.62 (FWC applications); filing a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d); improper filing of an RCE (e.g., without appropriate fee or required submission) which is treated as withdrawal of appeal; filing an RCE without a timely submission that meets 37 CFR 1.111 while a reply to a final Office action is outstanding; and improper RCE prior to payment of the issue fee (an improper RCE will not toll time for issue fee payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which proceedings on an earlier application are 'terminated' for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 120 (so that a later-filed application must be filed before termination to be copending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings terminate when (A) issue fee is not paid and application is abandoned for failure to pay (date of due payment is termination date), (B) application in interference loses as to all claims (proceedings terminated as of date appeal/review was due), (C) decision by the Board terminates proceedings, and (D) a decision by the court terminates proceedings. 'Before' means 'not later than.' See MPEP § 711.02(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between reconsideration of holding and revival
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may ask for reconsideration of an examiner's holding that an application was abandoned if they contend there was no abandonment in fact, versus filing a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 when there was abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may reverse a holding (treat application as never abandoned) if an amendment received during the reply period was responsive — this is not a revival. Where there is no dispute that the application is abandoned, a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 (with fee) is necessary for revival. See MPEP § 711.03(a)–(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw holding of abandonment (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a) is the correct route when applicant contends the application was never abandoned (e.g., dispute over sufficiency of reply or controlling dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a petition does not require a fee. It must generally be filed within two months of the action complained of (37 CFR 1.181(f)) or it may be dismissed as untimely. The Office may nevertheless treat an untimely petition on its merits if accompanied by terminal disclaimer in certain application types; intentional delay may lead to dismissal. The mere filing of a petition does not stay any periods for reply or other proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing required for nonreceipt of an Office action (petition basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: What evidence a practitioner must submit to support a claim that an Office communication was never received (for withdrawing a holding of abandonment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include a practitioner statement that the Office communication was not received and attest that a search of the file jacket and docket records indicates nonreceipt. Attach a copy of the docket record where the communication would have been entered and reference it (e.g., docket report showing replies for the relevant dates). Stronger proof may be required if practitioner has history of not receiving Office actions. Evidence of nonreceipt of other communications not directly tied to the reply-to-avoid-abandonment action will not necessarily warrant withdrawal. See Delgar v. Schulyer and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory bases and categories for revival (37 CFR 1.137 scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 provides revival for abandoned applications and lapsed patents for specific failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival covers failure to timely reply in a provisional, failure to timely prosecute nonprovisional applications, failure to timely pay the issue fee for design, utility, or plant applications, failure to timely pay any outstanding portion of the issue fee (lapsed patents), and failure to pay publication fee. Revival may be sought under 37 CFR 1.137(a) for unavoidable delay or 1.137(b) for unintentional delay, with differing documentary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content for unavoidable-delay revival (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for a grantable petition to revive based on unavoidable delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(l); (3) a showing satisfactory to the Commissioner that the entire delay from due date to petition filing was unavoidable; and (4) any terminal disclaimer required under 37 CFR 1.137(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content for unintentional-delay revival (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for a grantable petition to revive based on unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee per 37 CFR 1.17(m); (3) a statement that the entire delay from due date to petition filing was unintentional (Commissioner may request more info if in doubt); and (4) any terminal disclaimer required under 37 CFR 1.137(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply requirement for a revival petition (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by the 'required reply' — generally the reply that would have avoided abandonment if timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In many cases the required reply is the complete, proper reply to the outstanding Office action. For nonprovisional applications abandoned for failure to prosecute, required reply may be met by filing a continuing application or, for applications filed on/after June 8, 1995, an RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114. For abandonment for failure to pay issue/publication fees, the required reply must include payment of the fee or outstanding balance. See 37 CFR 1.137(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival when abandonment due to failure to pay issue or publication fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifics for applications abandoned for failure to pay issue or publication fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival requires submission of the issue fee or outstanding balance (per 35 U.S.C. 151 and 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7)). Filing a continuing application without payment of the issue fee is not an acceptable required reply for such abandonments. If issue fee increased, applicant must pay the balance. For publication-fee abandonment, revival requires payment of the publication fee even if revival is sought only to preserve continuity with a continuing application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply for abandonment after a non-final action
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes the required reply in a nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to reply to a non-final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required reply may be (A) an argument or amendment under 37 CFR 1.111, (B) filing a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or a CPA under 1.53(d) for certain older filings), or (C) other replies that would have been considered responsive. A petition may be granted if the reply appears bona fide; the examiner may later identify omissions and give a 1-month shortened period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to correct them (extensions under 1.136(a) permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply for abandonment after a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes the required reply in a nonprovisional application abandoned for failure to reply to a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required reply under 37 CFR 1.113 must include cancellation of, or appeal from, the rejection of each claim so rejected. Acceptable replies for petition purposes include: (A) a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee; (B) an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 that cancels all rejected claims or otherwise prima facie places the application in condition for allowance; (C) filing an RCE with submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114 (for utility/plant applications); or (D) filing a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (or CPA under 1.53(d) for certain older cases). When an amendment is proposed, the Office may route the case to the Technology Center to determine if the amendment places the application in condition for allowance; if not, the petition may be denied and PTOL-303 used to notify the Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reply when abandonment due to failure to file an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable replies where abandonment resulted from failure to file an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply must be either (A) an appeal brief complying with 37 CFR 1.192(c) with fee; (B) filing an RCE with submission and requisite fee for utility/plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995; or (C) filing a continuing application (or CPA for certain older filings). If a notice of appeal is used as the reply, the Commissioner will set the time for filing the appeal brief in the petition-decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using an RCE as the required reply for revival
rubrics_metrics.description: When an RCE may serve as the required reply to revive an application abandoned for failure to reply to a final action or to file an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For utility/plant applications, an RCE accompanied by a submission and fee can be the required reply. The submission must be responsive within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.111 to the last Office action (responsiveness determined without regard to the 'final' status). The submission may be a previously filed amendment after final or incorporate earlier arguments. Petition may be granted if submission appears bona fide; after revival, examiner may later find the reply lacking and give a 1-month shortened period under 37 CFR 1.135(c) to correct errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require continuing application or RCE instead of treating reply under 1.111/1.113
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances in which the Office can insist that the required reply be a continuing application or an RCE rather than a reply treated under 37 CFR 1.111 or 1.113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemplary circumstances include (A) application abandoned for an inordinate period, (B) application file contains multiple or conflicting replies to the last Office action, and (C) submitted replies under 37 CFR 1.137 appear questionable as to compliance with 37 CFR 1.111 or 1.113. In such cases, treating a reply under 1.111/1.113 may place an inordinate burden on the Office and a continuing application or RCE may be required (37 CFR 1.129(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for failure to notify Office of foreign filing after nonpublication request
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rule for nonpublication-requesting applicants who file abroad and fail to notify the USPTO within 45 days (35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nonprovisional application abandoned under 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) for failure to timely notify the Office of a foreign filing may be revived only on the basis of unintentional delay under 37 CFR 1.137(b) (not unavoidable delay). The reply requirement is met by the notification itself, but filing such a petition will not stay any other reply periods. The Office may continue to examine the application until notified of the failure to meet the 45-day notice requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition fee requirement and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When and which petition fee is required to revive an abandoned application or obtain acceptance of a delayed issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7), a petition to revive an unintentionally abandoned application or for unintentionally delayed payment of the issue fee must include the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(m), unless filed under 35 U.S.C. 133 or 151 (unavoidable delay) in which case the fee is 37 CFR 1.17(l). The fee is due on filing (not on grant); the Office will not consider the merits of a 37 CFR 1.137 petition lacking the requisite petition fee and the fee will not be refunded regardless of dismissal or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirements for revival petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a terminal disclaimer must accompany a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment or a petition to revive, and how the term dedication is calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137(d) in certain design applications and utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer and fee under 37 CFR 1.321 dedicating a terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment (or the lesser of the abandonment period and any period extending beyond 20 years from U.S. filing/earliest priority). The terminal disclaimer must also apply to any patent on a continuing application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c). Provisions do not apply where revival is sought solely for copendency with later applications filed on/after June 8, 1995, to lapsed patents, or to reexamination proceedings. A terminal disclaimer is sometimes required when Office treats an untimely petition on merits to avoid granting patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) due to prosecution delay caused by abandonment, because abandonment is a per se failure to exercise due diligence.
